# Pull Request: Minimalist Blog Website

## Summary

Build a same-origin minimalist blog application with account registration and login, server-side sessions, a searchable and sortable public feed, and author-protected post management. The implementation follows the approved requirements and architecture, and includes two targeted corrections identified during review so the documented Unicode password and maximum post-content limits work consistently.

## Changes Made

- `.gitignore` — excludes generated `node_modules/` and local `data/` database files from version control.
- `README.md` — documents the app, setup/run steps, validation defaults, security behavior, and deployment notes.
- `package.json`, `package-lock.json` — define the Node.js application scripts, runtime requirement, and dependencies.
- `server.js`, `db.js` — implement the HTTP application, validation, authentication/session handling, blog APIs, and SQLite persistence.
- `public/app.js`, `public/index.html`, `public/styles.css` — implement the client-side views, navigation, feed, search/sort, and post-management interface.
- `test/server.test.js` — adds one focused integration regression test for Unicode password limits, maximum-size CJK post content, and oversized-body handling.
- `artifacts/requirements.md` — records the approved functional and non-functional requirements.
- `artifacts/architecture.md` — describes the application architecture and implementation decisions.
- `artifacts/design-review.md` — records the design assessment and recommendations.
- `artifacts/impl-plan.md` — records prioritized implementation tasks and completion checks.
- `artifacts/code-review.md` — documents review findings, including the two P2 correctness issues.
- `artifacts/verification.md` — records initial verification, remaining acceptance gaps, and post-review correction checks.
- `artifacts/pr-description.md`, `artifacts/changelog.md`, `artifacts/review-checklist.md` — provide this PR package, the workflow changelog, and reviewer checklist.

The two P2 findings were fixed: browser password validation now counts Unicode code points consistently with the server, and the JSON body limit now accommodates the documented content maximum while oversized requests receive HTTP 413 rather than HTTP 500.

## Test Evidence

- `npm.cmd run check` — passed (Node syntax checks for `server.js`, `db.js`, and `public/app.js`).
- `npm.cmd test` — passed (1 focused integration regression test; 1 test, 0 failures).
- `git diff --check` — passed.

The focused test exercises Unicode password boundaries and maximum-size CJK content/oversized request handling. Browser acceptance and full acceptance-suite coverage have not been verified; this PR does not claim either.

## Known Limitations

- Browser-specific navigation, rendering, delete confirmation/cancellation, and UI interaction behavior have not been browser-tested.
- Automated coverage is focused on the two corrected P2 cases. Broader automated acceptance coverage for authentication, sessions, all search/sort modes, ownership, and UI flows remains incomplete.
- Production deployment behavior, HTTPS/proxy configuration, and performance at realistic feed volumes have not been independently validated.
- Image uploads, password reset/OTP, and rich-text editing remain out of scope.
